answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a garden as the anchor of the cost.
